SECTION A (30 MARKS)
1. Atomic Models
(a) Part labelled [+]: Nucleus
(b) Particle labelled e⁻: Electron
(c) Feature of Rutherford’s model:
The atom consists of a small, dense, positively charged nucleus surrounded by electrons orbiting at a distance (mostly
empty space).
(d) Isotope:
Atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
(e) Uses of isotopes:
 • Carbon-14 dating
 • Treatment of cancer (Cobalt-60)
 • Detecting leaks in underground pipes
(a) Identification:

iv. Hydrochloric acid: C (pH 1)
(b) Product of acid + metal:
Hydrogen gas and a salt
(c) Strong vs weak acids:
Strong acids fully ionize in water, while weak acids partially ionize.
